kill_argument: The claims are now honest, and that is what makes the case against the stage: they no longer support any positive decision about the return to schooling. H1 reproduced 5 of 9 primary targets; all four misses are in Card's Panel B columns 2 and 4 and are explained only by a post hoc regression (D4) that the approved plan did not contain. The one pre-registered decision about the return in Card's basic specification, H3(b), is 'not established' (robust projection set from about -0.007 to 0.498, statistic 7.30 at zero against 7.815). Everything that does come out positive (H3(a), H4, and H5's non-rejection) concerns the Panel A coefficient, which assumes experience exogenous, and H4's breakdown is the robust reduced-form lower limit restated. A hostile referee would call this a replication with caveats, not a robustness confirmation. The claims now say exactly that, so it limits what the paper may claim; it is not a defect in the claims. I attacked the revision: claim values, supports and macros are unchanged against HEAD (only texts changed and 13 claims were added); the new numbers follow from their metrics; the miss lists equal the verdict flags; validate is clean.
reviewer_checks_run: No estimation this round. Compared claims.jsonl with git HEAD: no claim removed, and no value, support, macro, format or kind changed. 15 texts changed and 13 claims added, matching the log entry at 19:20:10Z and runs/NOTES.md. Checked the arithmetic of the new claims from the run metrics: A5 clustered first-stage t^2 = 11.38 (below 16.38, 23.11 and the HC1 effective F 14.14); A6 t^2 = 19.01 (between 16.38 and 23.11); a6/a5 fs_se_cl / fs_se_hc1 = 0.916 / 1.115; young_iv - 1.959964 x young_iv_se = -0.031876 (code/r_age1419.py uses ivlib.Z975 with the conventional SE). The 7 'not reproduced' labels and the miss lists in h1-primary-reproduced and h1-secondary-reproduced equal the 0-flags in runs/verdict/metrics.json (B2 fs and SE, B4 rf and SE; B1 fs, B3 rf and SE; B1 SE reproduced). The rv-code-2 task is done. crew.py validate: OK, 0 warnings. My results-r1 recomputation (B6, A6 AR, CHR, H5 to 1e-9) still applies, because no value or run changed.

findings.text: The seed headline claim gave the replicated B6 coefficient the complier-return reading that the approved design rejects (iv-return: 'return ... for men whose schooling responds to proximity').
findings.resolution: Narrow the text to the design.estimand reading.
findings.response: Fixed: iv-return now gives the design.estimand reading (coefficient in this linear model, not the average return; the conditional weighted-average reading needs monotonicity and rich covariates, is not guaranteed here, and with experience instrumented by age the complier results do not define whose return it weights).
findings.ruling: Resolved. iv-return now reads 'the coefficient on schooling in this linear model, not the average return for all men'. It gives the conditional weighted-average reading only under monotonicity and rich covariates, says that this is not guaranteed on these data, and adds that, with experience instrumented by age, the complier results do not define whose return the coefficient weights. The text follows design.estimand. A smaller wording issue about Tubbicke remains; it is new finding F10.

findings.text: iv-return (and design.estimand, from which it is copied) says 'Tubbicke finds 2SLS well above estimators that do not rely on it' as evidence 'on these data' against the weighted-average reading of the per-year coefficient. Tubbicke's comparison uses a binary 'some college' treatment, without family background, n = 2,988, which is a different estimand (claims.jsonl c-tubbicke says so). The same claim also lists monotonicity as a condition, but cites evidence only against the covariate condition, although c-tubbicke reports Sloczynski's defier explanation. The Writer copies claim texts, so the paper's interpretation of its headline number would carry the unqualified version (literature-r2 L5 asked that Tubbicke be described as binary-treatment evidence).
